item.title: Impact of Environment and Emissions on Food Systems — Tue Nov 17, 12:00 PM — Trent Drive Hall 040
item.description:
Food systems everywhere are affected by changes in climate and our environments. Studies have shown that CO2 emissions reduce nutritional density on core crops. Shifting weather patterns affect planting and harvest cycles, while flooding and drought destroy crops and significantly reduce agricultural yield. Microplastics are increasingly identified throughout our food supply.
This Think Global panel will highlight some of the unexpected ways that our food systems are being impacted by a changing world. Panelists will share how food sources have been affected within the communities where they work, addressing both agricultural and manufacturing conditions that influence how critical nutrition is delivered.
Source: Duke University

item.title: From Developmental Signals to Butterfly Wing Diversity — Tue Nov 17, 12:30 PM — Nanaline Duke 147
item.description:
My research group examines how developmental systems generate morphological diversity and the mechanisms underlying its evolution. We work with butterflies and moths, which provide a rich comparative system for testing how changes in genomic regulation and gene regulatory networks underlie the evolutionary diversification of traits such as wing color patterns and wing shapes. We aim to pinpoint the genetic and developmental mechanisms that organize the wing as an organ at multiple levels, from the establishment of positional information to the growth and remodeling that shape the wing, and the specification of cell identities that produce structural and pigmentary coloration. Finally, we connect these genetic and developmental mechanisms to ecological function by investigating how complex wing phenotypes contribute to defense and mate choice.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Multi-Agent Playground — Tue Nov 17, 1:30 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description: The Multi-Agent AI Playground is a hands-on walkthrough that introduces you to agentic AI-systems where AI models take actions, use tools, and work together to accomplish tasks. Through seven progressively complex examples, you'll build your understanding step by step, starting with the basics and working up to more advanced setups. You'll start with simple LLM debates, where AI models argue a topic while another acts as judge, then see how a single agent can use tools like a calculator or web search through the ReAct pattern (Reason → Act → Observe). From there, you'll see how multiple agents can collaborate by sharing information, how a "manager" agent can delegate work to specialized helpers (for example, to build, test, and review a game), and how agents can plan multi-step tasks on their own and even spawn new sub-agents to get the job done. item.title: Triangle Nuclear Theory Colloquium - Nuclear Physics with Dynamical Pions: A Neural Quantum State Approach — Tue Nov 17, 1:30 PM — None
item.description:
Neural Quantum States (NQS) have emerged as a promising approach to solving the nuclear many-body problem, offering flexible representations of strongly correlated wave functions. However, most existing applications treat nucleons as the only explicit degrees of freedom, with pion dynamics encoded in effective nuclear interactions.
In this talk, I will discuss our ongoing efforts to extend the NQS framework to systems containing both nucleons and dynamical pion fields. Working within a low-energy effective theory, we construct variational wave functions that describe nucleons coupled to quantized pion modes in a finite periodic volume. I will present preliminary results for one- and two-nucleon systems, illustrating the application of this framework to nuclear dynamics with explicit pionic degrees of freedom.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Sat Feb 13, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math — Sun Feb 14
item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. item.title: SSRI Workshop: Intro to Power Analysis for Empirical Research (I): Why It Matters and How to Get Started — Tue Nov 17, 10:00 AM — SSRI-Gross Hall 270
item.description:
Intro to Power Analysis for Empirical Research (I): Why It Matters and How to Get Started November 17, 2026 | 10:00-11:30 a.m. LOCATION: Zoom
Figuring out the right sample size for empirical research is a balancing act: collecting too little data can lead to insufficient power to detect an effect, while oversampling can be costly. This introductory workshop will demystify the process of power analysis and introduce researchers to practical tools for making informed decisions about sample sizes.
The workshop will cover computational techniques relevant to commonly used research designs in the social sciences, including power analyses for moderation and mediation. It is designed for researchers who want a basic understanding of statistical power and how to apply power analysis to their own work.
Topics include:
~Understanding statistical power and why it matters ~Determining appropriate sample sizes for empirical research ~Using computational tools for power analysis ~Power analyses

item.title: Learning in Networks Reading Group — Tue Nov 17, 12:00 PM — Gross Hall
item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. By fostering collaboration across disciplines, the institute aims to develop new mathematical and algorithmic foundations for understanding complex networked systems and their applications. The institute is led by collaborators Jiaming Xu, Alex Belloni, Fan Wei, Galen Reeves, and James Moody. Learn more: https://sites.duke.edu/learninginnetworks/

item.title: BEAT: Belew/Vai/Levin/Bozzio Performing the Music of KING CRIMSON — Tue Nov 17, 7:30 PM — DPAC Presented by First Horizon
item.description:
Following more than 100 acclaimed performances across North and South America, Europe, and Japan, BEAT returns this fall for the last North American tour. Former King Crimson members Adrian Belew and Tony Levin are joined by guitar virtuoso Steve Vai and legendary drummer Terry Bozzio to perform the music of the three landmark 1980s King Crimson albums—Discipline, Beat, and Three of a Perfect Pair. Rather than attempting to recreate the original recordings, BEAT brings this extraordinary music to life with the spirit, precision, and adventurousness that made it so enduring. Whether you’ve lived with these albums for decades or are discovering them for the first time, this is the final opportunity to experience one of progressive music’s most celebrated catalogs performed by four of the best musicians on the planet.
Source: DPAC, Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Los Gaiteros De San Jacinto, Fruko, and Carmelo Torres Present Madre Cumbia! — Tue Nov 17, 8:00 PM — Motorco
item.description: Madre Cumbia portrait by @amandakazemiart MADRE CUMBIA — a historic collaboration between Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, Fruko, and Carmelo Torres. More than an album, Madre Cumbia brings together the living roots of Colombian cumbia with the artists who have carried, transformed, and preserved its legacy across generations. From the ancestral sounds of the gaitas and drums to the accordion of the sabanas and the electric bass that helped redefine tropical music, this record celebrates the full arc of cumbia’s evolution. Together, these artists embody nearly every chapter of cumbia’s recorded history—from its ceremonial Afro-Indigenous origins and rural accordion traditions to its electrification, international expansion, and enduring legacy. Madre Cumbia is more than a collaboration; it is a gathering of the musicians who have preserved, transformed, and carried one of Latin America’s most important musical traditions across generations. LOS GAITEROS DE SAN JACINTO Latin Grammy Award
